column1: # Fixture rep table for harness/test-recall-runner.sh (bead tla-wekw).
# This file pins the FORMAT recall/REPS.tsv uses. It is not the corpus; the
# real rep table is beads tla-1sh7.2's and tla-03ep.1's and is authored
# against this shape.
# BOTH ROW KINDS ARE HERE, four REP rows and three SPEC rows, and field 1 is
# which. The SPEC rows are at the bottom and their own section says what the
# three of them are for.
# A REP ROW. Rows are tab-delimited and carry the literal first field REP, so
# prose in this file can never be read as data. Six fields, and an optional
# seventh:
#   1  marker       the literal REP
#   2  id           stable, never renumbered
#   3  construct    K001-K105, resolving to a drill/INVENTORY.md row
#   4  environment  resolves to <env-dir>/<name>.tla
#   5  prompt       English, naming none of the notation it asks for
#   6  canonical    the answer, as TLA+
#   7  requires     OPTIONAL. An ERE the raw answer text has to match before a
#                   correct value is accepted. Absent or empty means no gate,
#                   and such a row grades exactly as it did before field 7
#                   existed, which is why R001 and R002 below still carry six.
#   awk -F'\t' '$1 == "REP" && $2 == "R001"' harness/fixtures/recall/REPS.tsv
# Four reps. R001's value is a set, so the value block counts it. R002's value
# is a function, so Cardinality errors and the count is skipped -- which is the
# case the fixture exists to exercise.
# R003 and R004 carry field 7, and they are the two shapes it has to survive.
# Both gate on the construct's OWN KEYWORD and on nothing else, because a
# pattern that reaches for the shape of the whole answer stops accepting the
# alternate spellings that make this rung gradeable without a model in the
# loop. The suite measures a correct alternate against each one.
REP
column5: the set of all the ways the wagons could be parked, one track each

column1: REP
column5: the parking that leaves every wagon on the first track

column1: REP
column5: for each track, twice its number, with the doubling given a name of its own rather than written out twice
column6: LET Twice(t) == t * 2 IN [t \in Tracks |-> Twice(t)]

column1: REP
column5: a count for each track, zero everywhere, after the first track alone has been set to nine

column1: # A SPEC ROW. Eight fields, and an optional ninth. Field 4 is a comma-
# separated list of scaffolds, each resolving to a PAIR under
# <env-dir>/spec/: <name>.tla and <name>.cfg. Field 7 is the same construct
# gate it is on a REP row. Field 8 is the vector of exit codes, one per
# scaffold. Field 9 fills the __CHECK__ hole of a scaffold that has one.
# THREE ROWS, AND EACH ONE IS A DIFFERENT SHAPE OF THE SAME MECHANISM:
#   Q001  one scaffold, keyed on one exit code. The fairness hole, where
#         the answer is the conjunct beside Init and the step relation
#   Q002  two scaffolds, keyed on the vector. The property hole, where one
#         run cannot grade the answer because a weaker property also
#         holds: fix-near is the machine it must hold on and fix-far the
#         machine it must fail on
#   Q003  one scaffold with a __CHECK__ hole, so field 9 has a subject.
#         The action hole, keyed on an INVARIANT in the scaffold and a
#         state-graph fingerprint in a POSTCONDITION
# Every number in field 8 and field 9 was measured on TLC2
# 2026.07.31.184830 on 2026-10-17, the way the CASES.tsv codes were.
SPEC
column5: the weaker promise about the counter's own step, enough that it cannot be left where it is while the flag carries on

column1: SPEC
column5: that the counter reaches two and from then on is never anywhere else

column1: SPEC
column5: a step that takes the counter up one while it has room, and leaves the flag reading what it read
